name: Rafael Young

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a usual shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and take the evening calls about utility bills at a contact centre. I finished secondary school and have only recently moved onto this desk, so I still ask a coworker to check a reversed payment. The evening allowance puts me toward the higher end of agent pay. I do not use AI tools; I need to get the ordinary account screen right first.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Elaine repairs clothing for a shop, and our children are grown and living elsewhere. We have about eight months of expenses saved, and several centres are close enough to reach. I like explaining one bill carefully and hearing the customer stop worrying. Retirement is on the horizon, but Elaine and I have not checked the income that would replace our wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the evening desk AI Plateau sounds like another small shortcut. I would still have someone check a reversed payment against the bill before saying it has cleared.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my shifts and evening allowance would stay. With eight months saved and several centres nearby, Elaine and I could handle an ordinary setback without rushing out of this job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking utility-bill calls and ask my coworker Hal to check two reversal dates with me during paid hours. In the first year of this small change, I’d keep that double check on cases I cannot settle myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about the wage. The bill can be settled slowly and still be settled correctly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which date did Hal show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week the account showed a reversal before the bank had posted the credit. Hal pointed to the later date before I told the caller the money was back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the reserve change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elaine (my partner) and I would leave the eight-month reserve for repairs and bills. A small screen change does not make it spending money.

say: I’d insist on a **reversal-date check** before promising a credit.
I’d say **small shortcuts** leave the evening desk paid.
think: I think my **evening allowance** remains in this picture.
I trust **eight months saved** and nearby centres for a normal setback.
do: Keep **utility-bill calls** and check two reversal dates with Hal on paid time.
Keep a **second account check** for unsettled cases in the first year.
S0.quote: The bill can be settled slowly and still be settled correctly.
fieldNote: His **higher pay** comes from an evening allowance, not senior standing.
He is **still learning** the current reversal dates with Hal.
The **existing reserve** is retained without a new saving pledge.

steps.text: Keep evening billing calls and check uncertain reversal dates with Hal

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues Steady Disruption will clear ordinary balance questions and leave us with the ones that come back angry. I would ask for the evening rota in writing before anyone talks about a new title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the experienced agents may get the remaining disputes while I lose some evening hours. Eight months saved gives us time to compare local centres, but the loss of a regular allowance would still hurt.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep practising difficult reversals with Hal on my paid shifts and request the next two rotas from my supervisor. In the first year easy calls move, if my evening hours fall, I’d check posted paid billing vacancies nearby for written weekly wages and hours that cover our bills after travel; I would leave only after a suitable offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the allowance, not interested in a course advert. I need to know how many paid evenings are actually left.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which rota number matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the number of paid late shifts, not just the total calls handled. One fewer evening can matter even if the hourly rate stays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a different journey cost?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elaine (my partner) and I would compare the new centre’s last bus with my finish time. A nominal raise would be wasted on rides home.

say: I’d ask for **written evening rotas** after ordinary calls move.
I’d distinguish **paid late shifts** from call totals.
think: I think **experienced agents** may keep the hard disputes.
I fear **losing evening allowance** even with eight months saved.
do: Keep **practising reversals** with Hal and request two paid rotas in 2026.
Check **posted nearby billing work** after hour cuts for written after-travel bill-covering weekly wages and hours.
Check the **last bus** against the new shift finish before leaving the current paid job.
S1.quote: One fewer evening can matter even if the hourly rate stays.
fieldNote: The **evening allowance** makes paid shift count important.
His supervisor request is **individual**, not a worker group demand.
A local move needs **written weekly net pay** and a last bus home.

steps.text: Keep practising difficult reversals with Hal and request two written evening rotas
Check posted billing vacancies with written after-travel bill-covering weekly wages/hours; leave only after signed offer
Check last bus against new shift finish before leaving current paid job

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2028 could answer a bill and check a reversal without an evening agent. Robots around 2031 are later; they do not keep my headset paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the centre could end most of my shifts quickly. Eight months saved and many local centres give Elaine and me room to search, but I have not proved we can retire on that reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for written notice of any shift cuts and check posted paid billing jobs at nearby centres. If my hours end in the first year after 2028, I’d apply only where written weekly wages and hours cover our bills after travel, keeping this job until a suitable offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious that I might lose most of a paid week. I can take time to look, but I cannot eat a job title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would another centre need to show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask whether the other centre actually pays for late shifts or only says the hourly rate is higher. I need the whole paid week, including evening shifts and travel costs, in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would Elaine check the journey?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elaine (my partner) would check the last bus and the finish time with me. We would not sign for a shift I cannot travel home from.

say: I’d ask for **written cut notice** before the evening rota changes.
I’d say **2028 AGI** reaches bill calls before robots.
think: I think **most evening shifts** could end fast.
I know **eight months saved** cannot prove we can retire.
do: Seek **written cut notice** and inspect posted nearby billing jobs in 2026.
Apply after lost hours for **posted paid work** with written after-travel bill-covering weekly wages and hours; leave when signed.
feel: **Anxious** that most paid shifts might disappear.
S2.quote: I need the whole paid week, including evening shifts and travel costs, in writing.
fieldNote: He fears a **large income loss** despite a strong buffer.
Other centres may offer a higher rate but **fewer paid shifts**.
The move needs a **signed offer** and a bus home.

steps.text: Inspect posted paid billing vacancies at nearby centres
Apply for posted work with written net bill-covering wages/hours; move on signed offer and last bus

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives me time to learn the difficult reversal calls properly before I decide whether to move. I would ask for a paid shift beside Hal, not an unpaid weekend class.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could get better at disputes if the centre keeps people to settle them. Full thinking AI may do those checks by 2031 too, so I would watch the paid rota instead of trusting a specialist label.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d keep taking billing calls and work one paid shift beside Hal on disputed reversals if the supervisor agrees. In the first year after 2031, if those hours disappear, I’d seek a posted paid disputes job nearby and move only on a signed offer with written weekly wages and hours covering bills after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but five years lets me practise disputed reversals at my current desk. Paid practice at my current desk is not a new career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Hal teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would watch Hal check when the bank and the centre each posted a reversal. That is the mistake I still make most often.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a specialist title?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elaine (my partner) and I would compare the new shift’s last bus and its full weekly wage. We would not move for a specialist title with fewer paid days.

say: I’d request a **paid shift beside Hal** to practise disputed reversals.
I’d ask for the **paid specialist rota** before trusting the title.
think: I think I can improve **current dispute work** with practice.
I know **2031 AGI** may still do those checks.
do: Keep **billing calls** and practise reversals beside Hal on paid time if approved.
Seek **posted disputes work** after 2031 if hours vanish; move only on signed written after-travel bill-covering weekly terms.
Require **full paid days** and a last bus home before moving to a disputes desk.
feel: **Uneasy**, with time to practise current work.
S3.quote: Paid practice at my current desk is not a new career.
fieldNote: His paid practice is **current-job coaching**, not retraining for another trade.
A specialist title needs **full paid days**, not a high rate alone.
The move needs **signed net weekly pay** and a last bus.

steps.text: Keep billing calls and practise disputed reversals beside Hal on paid time if approved
Seek posted disputes work if hours vanish; move only on signed after-travel bill-covering weekly wages/hours
Check full paid days and last bus against new shift finish before moving

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade, which is long enough to ask for real rotas each year. I would not claim every worker of 68 has stopped earning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think Elaine and I might have enough income to stop work by then, but we have not checked it. Full thinking AI could take bill calls in 2036, and robots around 2039 do not delay that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking the paid evening calls and ask Elaine to check our verified later-life income against regular bills. If I still need a wage after 2036 and the call hours fall, I’d inspect posted paid local jobs and move only on a signed offer with written weekly wages and hours covering bills after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but there is time to examine the numbers. Eight months in savings is not the same as income every month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What figures would you check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use actual pay letters and account statements before choosing a date. I do not know yet which income will continue after work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would grown children help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown children are building their own lives. I would not count their wages as part of ours unless they offered and the amount was clear.

say: I’d ask for **real yearly rotas** as 2036 approaches.
I’d say **age 68** does not prove work has ended.
think: I think we **might stop work** if verified income covers bills.
I know **2036 AGI** may still end my calls.
do: Keep **paid evening calls** and compare verified later-life income with regular bills.
Inspect **posted local jobs** only if wages remain needed after 2036 and call hours fall; move on signed after-travel bill-covering terms.
feel: **Uneasy**, with time to inspect the household figures.
S4.quote: Eight months in savings is not the same as income every month.
fieldNote: He does not assume a **retirement date** or pension amount.
The **eight-month reserve** differs from continuing monthly income.
Adult children’s **help is unpromised** and not budgeted.

steps.text: Keep paid evening calls and compare verified later-life income with regular bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could answer utility bills and take my evening allowance with the calls. Eight months saved and nearby centres give us a search window, but I still need paid work unless we confirm we can afford to stop. Written shift notice and a nearby role with a full week of pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: A person can be good at calming a caller and still be new to the billing screen. I want the hours written down before I decide whether a new role is worth the journey.

headlineQuote: A person can be good at calming a caller and still be new to the billing screen.
portrait: At **58**, Rafael is a junior utility-billing agent still learning after secondary school.
His **evening allowance** raises his pay, and he and Elaine have around eight months saved.
Their **grown children** live elsewhere, and several similar jobs are nearby.
He **never uses AI** and weighs full paid hours before any job move.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his evening-call wage before retirement income is known.
whatWouldHelp: **Written shift notice** and nearby paid work with enough full-week wages would help.
